message.content:
I don’t have real‑time market data, so I can’t give you the exact price for today.  Gold prices change every few seconds during trading hours, so the most reliable way to get the current U.S. spot price is to check a reputable financial news or commodities site such as:

- **Kitco** (https://www.kitco.com) – provides live gold pricing in U.S. dollars per ounce.  
- **Bloomberg** (https://www.bloomberg.com/markets/commodities) – offers up‑to‑minute gold quotes.  
- **Reuters** (https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities) – also publishes live gold prices.  
- **Investing.com** (https://www.investing.com/commodities/gold) – shows a live chart and current price.

If you need a quick snapshot, you can also look at the “Gold” ticker on most brokerage platforms (e.g., E*TRADE, Fidelity, Robinhood).  

For a rough idea, as of the last close before my knowledge cutoff (mid‑2024), U.S. spot gold was trading around **$1,950–$2,000 per ounce**.  However, that figure is only a historical reference; the actual price today could be higher or lower.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the gold price today in USA?" They want the current gold price. We cannot browse the internet. We can provide a general answer: gold price is around X per ounce, but we need to be careful. We can say approximate price or mention that it changes frequently. We can also provide a link to a reliable source. We should not fabricate. We can say "As of the last available data, the price was about $X per ounce." But we don't have real-time data. We can say "I don't have real-time data, but you can check websites like Kitco, Bloomberg, etc." That is safe.
